q: If I buy hydrogen made by electrolysis as an input, what does CBAM need from the supplier?
title: CBAM: electrolysis hydrogen as an input
short: Hydrogen routes with only electricity emissions give a direct figure of zero, but if you use that hydrogen as a precursor you must still name its production route. Using the zero as an actual value needs the producer's installation to be verified under CBAM rules, though a verifier may simplify the work, for example for hydrogen certified as RFNBO.
audience: Indian ammonia, DRI and steel producers planning to buy green hydrogen

p: For hydrogen as a CBAM good only direct emissions count, and electrolysis has minimal direct emissions. But a buyer who uses that hydrogen as a precursor claims an actual value of zero, and the guidance says that requires verification of the producing installation under CBAM rules.

sections.h: What to get from the supplier
ul: The producer's verification report for the production year.
The sector parameters and identity of the installation, as for any precursor.

p: Using a risk-based approach, verifiers may simplify the work for hydrogen free of direct emissions. The guidance gives an example: hydrogen certified as a renewable fuel of non-biological origin (RFNBO) under the EU Renewable Energy Directive, a certification needed to import green hydrogen under the EU's renewable energy framework.
If you make ammonia, hydrogen from a separate process such as electrolysis on your site is a precursor listed in Annex II. Its electricity emissions are then left out of the ammonia figure.
Until 2025, hydrogen certified under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/1184 could use a zero electricity factor. In the definitive period hydrogen's electricity emissions are not counted at all.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills and purchase invoices into dated records for a plant that buys or makes hydrogen. It does not issue hydrogen certificates or verify a producer's route.
